title: Assessing Cases based on Hoarding Management Framework
what_it_is: Assessing Cases based on Hoarding Management Framework

sections.label: HDB hoarding fire hazard questions
sections.summary: Questions ask whether agencies will step up inspections, issue decluttering notices, and update on the multi-agency hoarding workgroup's efforts in HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: asked the Minister for National Development in view of the recent spate of home fires in HDB estates, whether HDB, SCDF or the relevant agencies will step up inspections and consider issuing decluttering notices to homes with excessive hoarding that pose serious fire hazard risks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: asked the Minister for National Development whether an update can be provided on efforts by the multi-agency workgroup in coordinating hoarding cases under the Hoarding Management Framework to reduce fire hazards in HDB flats.

sections.label: MHA questions relevant to MND
sections.summary: Questions 23 to 26 on fire risk in HDB flats are directed to MHA and are relevant to the MND Parliamentary Questions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Third, Question Nos 23 to 26 on today's Order Paper on the issue of fire risk in HDB flats, which are directed to MHA, have a bearing on and are relevant to, the MND Parliamentary Questions (PQs).

sections.label: Hoarding Management Core Group
sections.summary: The Hoarding Management Core Group, led by the Municipal Services Office, was set up in 2014 to coordinate agencies and resolve severe hoarding cases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The Hoarding Management Core Group (HMCG), led by the Municipal Services Office (MSO), was set up in 2014 to coordinate efforts across agencies and resolve protracted and severe hoarding cases.

sections.label: Hoarding cases reduced and monitored
sections.summary: As of the first half of 2022, HMCG reduced the severity of 210 hoarding cases and is monitoring them, with 260 active cases being worked on.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Nevertheless, HMCG has achieved some success, and as of the first half of 2022, we have managed to reduce the severity of 210 cases of hoarding and are actively monitoring these cases to prevent recurrence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Agencies are currently working on another 260 active hoarding cases.

sections.label: Stepping up corridor enforcement
sections.summary: Agencies are committed to reviewing enforcement levers and plan to work with Town Councils to step up enforcement on cluttered corridors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: To this end, agencies are committed to reviewing enforcement levers and acting more decisively on decluttering efforts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We plan to intensify actions to keep corridors clear for passage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: In the coming months, agencies intend to work with Town Councils to step up enforcement on cluttered corridors.
